panels.title: Today's Q7
points: Compare how the writers present their experiences of an extraordinary machine.
Support with references to both texts

model.title: Compare how the writers present their experiences.

parts.text: Point: both feel awe and dare to get close
Evidence: 'I did push it' / 'very near the platform's edge'
Methods: confessional first person in both
Perspective: one touches the past, one meets the new
Judgement: both turn a machine into a personal moment

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Both writers dare to come close to the machines that awe them: the modern visitor confesses 'I did push it' when the guide is not looking, and the letter-writer stood 'very near the platform's edge'. Yet their perspectives differ: one touches a machine that is now history, while the other meets the future arriving.

keywords.def: both texts discussed in the same sentences

questions.q: Fill the plan grid with one more idea
questions.a: For example: the effect on other people: the guide versus the whole town.
For example: 'The lens is calm and still, whereas the engine is loud and alive.'

questions.q: Core (timed, 20 minutes): in the portal response box, answer Q7. Starter: 'Both writers...'
questions.a: Mark scheme points: shared awe and daring; perspective of a modern visitor to history versus a nineteenth-century witness of something new; methods: metaphor of the beehive and the creature; confessional first person; structure ending in personal feeling; integrated with connectives and a judgement.

questions.q: Extend: self-mark with the Q7 ladder
Stretch: add one sentence on how context shapes each perspective
questions.a: For example: the letter-writer has never seen a machine move without a horse.

options: Both writers are awed by a machine, but one meets its history while the other meets its future.
